# Security, Idempotency and Pinned Versions Checklist: Environment Features

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for secrets, repeat installs and version pinning are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before `/speckit-tasks`.
**Created**: 2026-11-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Depth: standard. Audience: reviewer of the spec and plan pull request. Scope: tailnet, node-guard, ts7-cli, and the verify and release changes. Excluded: Tailscale ACLs, tag owners, arm64.

## Secrets and Auth Key Handling

- [x] CHK001 Is "the key never enters an image layer" extended to build arguments, Feature options, `options.env` and Docker image labels, and not only to `RUN` output? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003] Evidence: spec.md FR-003 lists image layer, build argument, Feature option value, file or label, image environment, and says `authKeyVar` holds a name.
- [x] CHK002 Is the place where the key may exist at runtime (process environment, key file, command line) specified, with the exposure window for each? [Gap, Plan Slice 4] Evidence: spec.md FR-026 allows the key only in the process environment and one root-only file during one `tailscale up`, and bars the command line.
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec require the key file to be removed on every exit path of the join, including a failed `tailscale up`? [Coverage, Plan Slice 4] Evidence: spec.md FR-026 says the key file is removed on every exit path; tasks.md T033 adds a trap.
- [x] CHK004 Is "a missing key logs one line" defined for a variable that is set but empty? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-007] Evidence: spec.md FR-007 and the first Edge Cases bullet say unset or empty.
- [x] CHK005 Is the log content restricted so that no key value or key fragment can appear in `/var/log/tailnet.log` or in the `tailscaled` log? [Gap, Spec §FR-006] Evidence: spec.md FR-026 bars the key from tailnet logs and says the key reaches `tailscale` only through the file, so the `tailscaled` log gets none from tailnet.
- [x] CHK006 Is AC3 specific about what "the repo secrets scan" scans, which key pattern it matches, and how a canary value proves the scan can fail? [Measurability, Spec §AC3] Evidence: spec.md FR-027 names the canary, the `tskey-` prefix, the three scan targets and a planted-canary negative control; SC-003 repeats it.
- [x] CHK007 Are file mode and owner requirements stated for the log file, the key file and `options.env`? [Gap, Plan Technical Context] Evidence: spec.md FR-028 gives root ownership and modes 0644 (options file, log) and 0600 (key file).
- [x] CHK008 Is the requirement for the upstream Tailscale Feature, which receives the same key and joins first, stated as an accepted exposure rather than left implicit? [Dependency, Research §R3] Evidence: spec.md Assumptions state that the upstream Feature reads `TS_AUTH_KEY`, joins first and that the exposure is accepted.
- [x] CHK009 Are the allowed characters for `authKeyVar`, `tags` and `hostnamePrefix` written as requirements, given that the values are sourced from a shell file? [Gap, Data Model] Evidence: spec.md FR-029 lists the allowed values for `tags`, `authKeyVar`, `hostnamePrefix`, `ssh` and `version`.
- [x] CHK010 Are requirements defined for a key that is expired, revoked or lacks the tag owner rights, so the failure is logged and not fatal? [Exception Flow, Spec §FR-006] Evidence: spec.md FR-006 and the Edge Cases bullet on expired, revoked or tag-refused keys require a log line and a normal start.
- [x] CHK011 Is it stated that the node keeps `tag:devcontainer` only when the tailnet policy allows it, and who owns that policy? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] Evidence: spec.md Assumptions say Dru owns the tailnet policy, ACLs are out of scope and a refusal is logged.

## Idempotency and Restart Behaviour

- [x] CHK012 Is "leaves the same result" in AC6 defined by named artefacts (files, modes, owners, links, installed versions) that a second run must leave unchanged? [Clarity, Spec §AC6] Evidence: spec.md FR-030 defines same result as same paths, owners, modes, content, links and package versions.
- [x] CHK013 Does the spec define the result when the second run uses different option values from the first? [Coverage, Gap] Evidence: spec.md FR-030 and the Edge Cases bullet say a second run with other options equals a fresh install with them.
- [x] CHK014 Is the idempotency requirement stated for the entrypoint (container restart), and not only for `install.sh`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008] Evidence: spec.md FR-030 last sentence and FR-008 cover the entrypoint on restart.
- [x] CHK015 Are requirements defined for a restart where the saved Tailscale state holds another hostname, another tag set or `--ssh` off? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008] Evidence: spec.md FR-008, US1 scenario 5 and the Edge Cases bullet cover another hostname, other tags and SSH off.
- [x] CHK016 Does the spec say what happens when two entrypoint runs overlap, for example a fast restart while the first join is still running? [Gap, Exception Flow] Evidence: spec.md FR-036 and the Edge Cases bullet on overlapping runs say the second run logs one line and stops.
- [x] CHK017 Is the behaviour defined when the workspace folder name changes between runs? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases] Evidence: spec.md Edge Cases bullet on a folder name that changes between runs says the next start applies the new hostname.
- [x] CHK018 Is it stated that an upgrade of the `version` option replaces the previous TypeScript install, with no leftover package? [Gap, Spec §FR-015] Evidence: spec.md FR-015 last sentence and US3 scenario 3 say a version change replaces the install and leaves no file of the old one.
- [x] CHK019 Do the requirements for an unsupported base state that nothing is written before the check fails? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020] Evidence: spec.md FR-020 says the unsupported-base failure comes before any write or install.

## Pinned Versions

- [x] CHK020 Is "the default is a tested version" backed by a requirement that names how the tested version is recorded and kept equal to the default? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015] Evidence: spec.md FR-031 names the tested versions and the `fast` check that keeps `DEFAULT_*` constants equal to the JSON defaults; FR-023 defines tested.
- [x] CHK021 Are the pins for `ghcr.io/tailscale/codespace/tailscale` and `ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node` specified (tag, digest or major), and is the upstream `latest` Tailscale default addressed? [Gap, Research §R3] Evidence: spec.md FR-031 requires an exact `version` option and the major tag on each `dependsOn`; research.md R3 and R5b record the pins and the upstream defaults.
- [x] CHK022 Is the integrity requirement for the TypeScript download stated (registry lockfile, checksum or none), given Constitution IV pins the version but not the content? [Gap, Spec §FR-015] Evidence: spec.md FR-031 says npm and the Tailscale package host supply integrity and no extra checksum is required.
- [x] CHK023 Is the rule for `version=latest` consistent between the spec, the constitution and the option description text? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015] Evidence: spec.md FR-015 and FR-031 agree: `latest` only by explicit choice and untested; matches Constitution IV.
- [x] CHK024 Is the requirement that the version string is validated before use stated, with the accepted forms listed? [Completeness, Data Model] Evidence: spec.md FR-029 lists the accepted `version` forms and requires one error line per bad value.
- [x] CHK025 Is the Feature `version` bump rule defined for every change that must reach users, including the orca-server `installsAfter` line? [Gap, Spec §FR-025] Evidence: spec.md FR-032 states the bump rule and FR-025 applies it to orca-server (1.0.2).
- [x] CHK026 Is the pinned `@devcontainers/cli` version, which defines "tested", named as a dependency of AC8? [Dependency, Spec §AC8] Evidence: spec.md FR-023 ties tested to the `@devcontainers/cli` version that `verify.sh` pins.
- [x] CHK027 Does the spec define how a drifting upstream (Tailscale or Node Feature changing behaviour under a pinned major tag) is detected? [Gap, Assumption] Evidence: spec.md FR-031 pins every dependency and says upstream drift is detected by `verify.sh ci` failing.

## Verification Coverage

- [x] CHK028 Does AC8 define "tests every Feature" so a Feature that has no `scenarios.json` or no host-side test is a stated case and not a silent skip? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022] Evidence: spec.md FR-022 and US4 scenario 4 make `fast` fail for a Feature without `test.sh` or `scenarios.json`, and state when host scripts run.
- [x] CHK029 Is the constant-equals-default check required for every Feature with a pinned default, in the spec and not only in the plan? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022] Evidence: spec.md FR-031 requires the constant check for any option with a default constant; tasks.md T005 builds it.
- [x] CHK030 Is AC1 reconciled with the fact that CI has no tailnet and no tun device, with the proof level for CI and for manual runs written down? [Conflict, Spec §AC1] Evidence: spec.md FR-033 defines the two proof levels for AC1: stub in CI and one dated manual run.
- [x] CHK031 Is the AC10 wording ("triggers on a change to any path under src/") consistent with a workflow that triggers on every push to main? [Conflict, Spec §AC10] Evidence: spec.md FR-024 says release.yaml triggers on every push to main, which includes `src/`, and that any `paths` filter must list `src/**`.

## Notes

- Items are reviewer-owned. `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state and does not change markers.
- CHK030 and CHK031 point at differences already recorded in `plan.md`. Close them by amending the spec text or accepting the plan note.
